grand_strategy.reading:
Republika Srpska is an entity of a state that it works to hollow out, run by a
party that kept the entity three times in a year in which its leader lost his
office. Its grand strategy is the strategy of a sub-state actor whose
patron needs it loud but not detached: Belgrade wants a Republika Srpska strong
enough to hold Bosnia hostage to the Serbian cause and keep the Sarajevo
state weak, but not so detached that Serbia must either own a secession or
disown a kin. That makes the entity's best move the threat, not the act - and
here Luttwak's paradoxical logic bites hardest. Each time Banja Luka has
crossed the line (the laws of 27 Feb 2025) the state's institutions have
reacted (court annulment, EUFOR reserve troops, entry bans, the High
Representative's funding cut), and those institutions came out stronger and
better tested than before; the repeal of 18 Oct 2025 was a retreat that
Washington rewarded within eleven days. The lesson Banja Luka drew is not
restraint but timing: escalate, absorb, retreat for a price, and let paid
lobbyists and a weaker OHR (Schmidt out in May 2026, an acting High
Representative from 1 July) do the rest.

Signals that are not rows. The plea agreement and the pardon: no source reached
shows a plea agreement between Dodik and the State Prosecutor's Office, and
the prison term was converted into a fine of about EUR 18,660 on 12 Aug 2025
at the defence's request, the six-year ban untouched; in October 2026
Bosnian media discuss whether the state Presidency could pardon him, which
would need all three members and the prior opinion of the State Court - a
debate, not an act. Orban's defeat in April 2026 removes the entity's best
door in the EU, and no source on the new Hungarian government's line toward
Banja Luka was found. The entity's two stable patrons are therefore
Belgrade (kin, bounded) and Moscow (kin, expensive); its transactional ones
are Washington, Budapest, Jerusalem, Ankara and Beijing, none of which has a
treaty with it.
